title: Google Suite
content:
## Overview

Google Suite integration allows your Emergent app to access Google services including Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace products. This integration uses OAuth 2.0 for secure authentication and requires configuration in the Google Cloud Console.

<Note>
Before configuring Google Suite, ensure you have a Google Cloud project and billing enabled. Some Google APIs require a verified domain for production use.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

- A Google Cloud account with a project created
- Admin access to your Emergent app
- The specific Google APIs enabled that you plan to use (Gmail API, Calendar API, Drive API, etc.)

## Setup Process

<Steps>

<Step title="Enable Google APIs">
Navigate to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com) and select your project. In the **APIs & Services** section, enable the specific Google APIs your app needs:

- **Gmail API** — for email operations
- **Google Calendar API** — for calendar access
- **Google Drive API** — for file storage and management
- **Google Docs/Sheets/Slides API** — for document operations

Click **Enable API** for each service you require.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure OAuth consent screen">
In the Google Cloud Console, go to **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**:

1. Choose **External** user type (or **Internal** if using Google Workspace)
2. Enter your app name, user support email, and developer contact
3. Add authorized domains (include your Emergent app domain)
4. Configure scopes based on the APIs you enabled
5. Add test users if your app is in testing mode

<Warning>
Apps in testing mode are limited to 100 test users. Submit for verification to remove this limit and make your integration available to all users.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Create OAuth credentials">
Navigate to **APIs & Services → Credentials** and create OAuth 2.0 credentials:

1. Click **Create Credentials → OAuth client ID**
2. Select **Web application** as the application type
3. Add authorized redirect URIs — use the callback URL provided in your Emergent integration settings
4. Save and note your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to Emergent">
In your Emergent app dashboard, navigate to **Integrations → Google Suite**:

1. Paste your Google OAuth **Client ID**
2. Paste your Google OAuth **Client Secret**
3. Select which Google services to enable
4. Save the configuration

Your app will now use these credentials to authenticate users via Google.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Trigger the Google authentication flow in your app to verify the setup:

1. Click the sign-in or connect button in your app
2. You should be redirected to Google's consent screen
3. Grant the requested permissions
4. Verify you're redirected back to your app with access granted

Check your app logs for any authentication errors.
</Step>

</Steps>

## Service-Specific Configuration

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Gmail">
The Gmail API requires the following scopes for common operations:

- `gmail.readonly` — read-only access to messages
- `gmail.send` — send email on behalf of the user
- `gmail.modify` — read and modify (but not delete) messages
- `gmail.compose` — create and send drafts

Configure these scopes in your OAuth consent screen under **Scopes**.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Google Calendar">
For calendar integration, add these scopes:

- `calendar.readonly` — read-only calendar access
- `calendar.events` — read and write calendar events
- `calendar` — full calendar access

Calendar API supports event creation, updates, deletion, and real-time sync.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Google Drive">
Drive API scopes control file access levels:

- `drive.readonly` — read-only access to all files
- `drive.file` — access only to files created by your app
- `drive` — full Drive access
- `drive.metadata.readonly` — read file metadata only

<Tip>
Use the most restrictive scope that meets your needs. Users are more likely to grant limited permissions.
</Tip>
</Tab>

<Tab title="Docs, Sheets & Slides">
Document APIs share similar scope patterns:

- `documents.readonly` / `spreadsheets.readonly` / `presentations.readonly`
- `documents` / `spreadsheets` / `presentations` — full access
- `drive.file` — access to files created by your app

These APIs allow programmatic creation and editing of Google Workspace documents.
</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Common Issues

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Redirect URI mismatch error">
This occurs when the callback URL in your Emergent settings doesn't match the authorized redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console. Ensure the URLs match exactly, including the protocol (`https://`) and trailing slashes.

Copy the exact redirect URI from your Emergent integration settings and paste it into the Google Cloud Console authorized URIs list.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Access blocked: App not verified">
Google displays this warning for unverified apps requesting sensitive scopes. During development, click **Advanced → Go to [App Name] (unsafe)** to proceed.

For production apps, submit your OAuth consent screen for Google verification. This process can take several weeks.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Insufficient permissions / 403 errors">
Verify that:

1. The required API is enabled in Google Cloud Console
2. The necessary scopes are configured in your OAuth consent screen
3. Users have granted all requested permissions during authentication
4. Your Google Cloud project has billing enabled (required for some APIs)
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Quota exceeded errors">
Google APIs have usage quotas and rate limits. Check your quota usage in the Google Cloud Console under **APIs & Services → Dashboard**.

Request quota increases if you're hitting limits, or implement rate limiting and caching in your app.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

## Best Practices

- **Request minimal scopes** — only ask for permissions your app actively uses
- **Handle token refresh** — OAuth tokens expire; implement refresh logic
- **Store tokens securely** — never expose access tokens in client-side code
- **Respect rate limits** — implement exponential backoff for API requests
- **Use service accounts** — for server-to-server operations without user authentication
- **Monitor quota usage** — track API consumption to avoid unexpected quota exhaustion
